title: Hamlet's Mill on ancient knowledge of precession

tellings.quote: very ancient very early knowledge of of precession.

plain: Ancient peoples had "very ancient very early knowledge" of precession, the slow wobble of the Earth that shifts the stars over thousands of years, according to the book Hamlet's Mill, written in the 1960s by the historian of science Giorgio de Santillana of MIT and the scholar Hertha von Dechend of Frankfurt University. The writer Graham Hancock cites the book on Michels's show. If true, it would mean early cultures tracked the sky with far more skill than usually believed.
